chunks: Ahmad, from his father, from Suleyman Al-Ja'fari, who said:

Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'Sometimes when the meal is brought, one of the people intends to wash his hand, so he (peace be upon him) would say: 'The one whose hand is clean, there is no harm in him eating without washing his hand.'

key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it necessary to wash hands before eating if they are already clean?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies the distinction between general cleanliness and the ritual act of washing specifically for prayer, ruling that a clean hand suffices for eating without requiring a fresh ablution. This reflects the Shia juristic principle that minor impurities do not invalidate eating, emphasizing practical ease (*rukhas*) in daily sustenance while maintaining hygiene. The narration underscores the flexibility in fiqh regarding bodily purity for non-worship activities, contrasting with the stricter requirements for Salah.

en.hubeali: Ahmad, from his father, from Suleyman Al Ja’fary who said,

‘Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> said, when sometimes they come with the meal, so one of the people intended to wash his hands, so he<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘The one whose hands are clean, so there is no problem if he were to eat without washing his hands’.
en.sarwar: 13. Ahmad has narrated from his father from Sulayman al-Ja‘fariy who has said the following: “
Abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, when food was made available and certain people had not washed their hands, would say, ‘Those whose hands are clean can eat without washing their hands.’”
